cur:catacombs-arles-good-shepherd-fragme.summary: In this fragment the Good Shepherd stands among bearded apostles, a sheep across his shoulders, between trees with spreading branches. Here the shepherd figure has been absorbed into a Gospel scene with the apostles, making its reference to Christ explicit.
facts: The museum describes it as a fragment of a sarcophagus showing the Good Shepherd with the sheep on his shoulders.

cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: Below the text 'Why do the heathen rage … against the Lord, and against his anointed (Christum eius)', the haloed Christ stands calmly between a crowd of armed men with spears on the left and a man who gestures toward him on the right. The miniature reads the psalm as a prophecy of the conspiracy against Christ in his Passion.
facts: Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
The manuscript came to Württemberg under Duke Charles Eugene (its sale is first mentioned in 1787) and has been in the library at Stuttgart since at least 1818.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature.
